note: The systems the New Machine assistant offers to download (docs/VIRTUALIZATION.md 4.1 and 3.9, "The Linux download cards"). Read by the app (apps/machines/catalog.js, bundled) and by the admin helper as root (server/src/vm/vmcatalog.c, from /usr/lib/lordos/assets/machines/systems.json): JS names an entry and an architecture, never a URL. An entry names a release, not a file: 'dir' is the maker's folder for it, 'sums' the maker's own SHA-256 list in that folder (or 'sumsPattern', the list's name to look for in the folder's listing when the name changes per build), and 'file' the image's name as an extended regular expression; the newest matching name in the list is taken, and the download must have the SHA-256 the list gives for it, or it is thrown away. 'fileDir' is where the image itself is fetched when it isn't 'dir' (a mirror redirector). 'approxMb' is only what the card says before the list is read; 'maxMb' is the most a download may be. 'hashSource' says where each hash comes from; 'checked' is when the entry was last tried. Order is the cards' order.

systems.name: Debian
systems.hashSource: SHA256SUMS published by Debian next to the images (cdimage.debian.org, current release); the list's OpenPGP signature (SHA256SUMS.sign) is not checked yet

systems.name: Ubuntu
systems.hashSource: SHA256SUMS published by Canonical in the release folder (releases.ubuntu.com for amd64, cdimage.ubuntu.com for arm64); the list's OpenPGP signature (SHA256SUMS.gpg) is not checked yet

systems.name: Fedora
systems.hashSource: the CHECKSUM file published by Fedora in the release folder (dl.fedoraproject.org; its name changes per build, so it is found in the folder's listing); it is OpenPGP clear-signed, and the signature is not checked yet

systems.name: Kali
systems.hashSource: SHA256SUMS published by Kali in cdimage.kali.org/current; the list's OpenPGP signature (SHA256SUMS.gpg) is not checked yet
